thesis.coreBelief: CEG compounds to $360+ over 24 months as the 1,121 MW AI nuclear PPA begins revenue in June 2027, the Crane Clean Energy Center restarts, and $8.4B of 2026–27 FCF funds buybacks and dividend growth — repricing the stock from a utility multiple to a contracted infrastructure multiple.
keyAssumptions: The 1,121 MW largest AI nuclear PPA commences revenue as contracted in June 2027, with no material counterparty default or contract restructuring by the hyperscaler buyer.

The Crane Clean Energy Center (Three Mile Island Unit 1) restarts in 2027 on schedule, adding ~835 MW of nuclear generation under the Microsoft PPA without a multi-quarter delay driven by grid interconnection or federal waiver failure.
CEG delivers $8.4B of cumulative FCF in 2026–27, confirming that the Calpine integration has not structurally impaired the company's cash generation capacity.
Nuclear IRA production tax credits remain in force, providing the per-MWh floor that underpins PPA economics and protects downside in a merchant-price downturn.
invalidationConds: A hyperscaler counterparty restructures, cancels, or materially delays the 1,121 MW AI PPA beyond H2 2027, removing the single largest forward revenue inflection from the model.
The Crane Clean Energy Center restart slips beyond Q1 2028, signaling systemic grid interconnection or regulatory failure that calls the entire nuclear restart pipeline into question.

CEG reports two consecutive quarters of guidance cuts driven by Calpine integration cost overruns or margin compression — defined as EPS actuals more than 10% below the $11–$12 2026 guidance range in back-to-back quarters.
The nuclear IRA production tax credits are materially repealed or curtailed via legislation, removing the economic floor that makes long-duration nuclear PPAs viable at premium pricing.
